sara: Hey infra team — quick QA on a Terraform/Gateway change in staging. Opening PR 1432 to move inference svc from NodePort -> ClusterIP and wire TLS via Gateway + SecretBinding. After the change the NLB healthchecks started returning 502s and the gateway backend is showing unhealthy. Anyone seen this pattern when switching to ClusterIP + gateway secret in a different namespace?

sara: repro snippets from the PR:```hcl
resource "kubernetes_service" "inference" {
  metadata { name = "inference-svc" namespace = "inference" }
  spec {
    type = "NodePort"
    ports { port = 8080 target_port = 8080 node_port = 31080 }
    selector = { app = "inference" }
  }
}
```and the proposed Gateway SecretBinding (we keep certs in infra-certs ns):```yaml
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1alpha2
kind: SecretBinding
metadata:
  name: inference-tls-binding
spec:
  secretRef:
    name: inference-cert
    namespace: infra-certs
```Main symptoms: LB health shows success -> then 502 when routing, pods show Ready, readiness probe on :8080 passes locally.

jon: quick thought — two things to check: 1) if the LB healthcheck is hitting nodeport and you removed NodePort, it may be hitting the wrong port. 2) Gateway/SecretBinding semantics: some gateway implementations expect the SecretBinding (or the secret) to be in the same namespace as the Gateway or require RBAC to allow cross-ns secret refs.

jon: can you paste the Service after the change and the Gateway config? also which gateway impl in staging (contour/gateway-api-controller/aws-load-balancer-controller)?

sara: staging uses gateway-api with aws-load-balancer-controller (NLB). After PR Service is ClusterIP, Gateway is in namespace ingress-gateway while certs live in infra-certs. Service now looks like:```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-svc
  namespace: inference
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 8080
      targetPort: 8080
  selector:
    app: inference
```Gateway uses TLS passthrough to the backend (tcp).

kevin: for NLB + targetType=Node you usually need a NodePort to anchor the healthcheck. If aws-lb-controller created an NLB pointing at nodes, healthchecks will call the nodeport. When you switch to ClusterIP the nodeport goes away and the ALB/NLB healthcheck target port disappears -> unhealthy.

kevin: options: A) keep NodePort but avoid exposing the NodePort publicly (set externalTrafficPolicy/local? and LB annotations) B) use targetType=IP on the service/gw so LB targets pod IPs directly, or C) add the annotation to tell the controller which healthcheck port to use. For example: `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-port: "tcp:8080"` (or the numeric node port).

jon: on the SecretBinding: aws-load-balancer-controller requires the cert secret in the same ns as the Gateway (I ran into this). Either copy the secret into ingress-gateway namespace, or create a SecretBinding resource in the gateway ns that references the secret (but check controller docs). If you try cross-namespace secretRef without controller support you'll get no TLS applied and weird failures.

sara: nice — that matches what I suspected. Two follow-ups: 1) should we prefer targetType=IP so we can keep ClusterIP service and avoid nodeports? 2) if we copy the secret into ingress-gateway ns, do we have automation for that (avoid manual sync)?

kevin: targetType=IP is cleaner if your controller supports it and you want pod-level targets. downside: requires CNI + security groups allowing pod IPs (works in our staging). If you go that route update the Service annotations and the Ingress/Gateway to request targetType=ip.

kevin: for secret sync we have an existing script in infra-scripts to mirror certs to the ingress ns via a CI job — see docs/ops/cert-sync (I can add a job to run on PR merge).

jon: short-term fix: copy secret into ingress ns and add the healthcheck annotation so NLB hits 8080. Long-term: switch to targetType=IP + ClusterIP services, update security groups.

sara: I'll update PR: add cert copy job and keep ClusterIP + add `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-port: "8080"` annotation for staging. Also will open follow-up ticket for targetType=IP rollout. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1432 :eyes:

infra-bot: deploy-canary: PR 1432 -> staging started (canary=1/3).

kevin: :thumbsup: I'll add a note in the PR about the secret sync job and reference the ops script.

sara: thanks — I'll push the annotation + a small kube job to copy secret on merge, then re-run canary and ping you if any more 502s show up.

infra-bot: deploy-canary: PR 1432 -> staging completed (canary=3/3) :white_check_mark:
